definition.name: web_search
definition.description: Search the public web for current information, news, standards or documentation. Returns a short list of results (title, url, snippet) — not full pages. Use web_extract on the most relevant urls to read them. Cite the urls you rely on.

query.description: Search query, as you would type it into a search engine

max_results.description: Number of results to return (1-10, default 5)

region.description: Optional region code to localise results, e.g. "us-en", "uk-en", "vn-vi"

max_results.description: Number of results to return (1-7, default 3)

region.description: Optional region code to localise results, e.g. "us-en", "uk-en", "vn-vi"

region.description: Optional region code to localise results, e.g. "us-en", "uk-en", "vn-vi"

definition.name: web_extract
definition.description: Fetch one or more public web pages (http/https) and return their readable text content. Use after web_search to read the most relevant results, or for a url the user gave you. Supports HTML, plain text, JSON and XML; not PDFs or binaries. Long pages are truncated.

max_chars.description: Max characters of text returned per page (default 20000, max 50000)

max_chars.description: Max characters of text returned per page (default 4000, max 8000)

definition.name: clarify
definition.description: Ask the user a clarifying question and wait for their answer. Use only when the request is genuinely ambiguous or missing information you cannot find with other tools, and a wrong guess would waste work. Ask one focused question; optionally offer up to 4 short choices (the user may still answer in their own words).

question.description: The question to ask the user

definition.name: skill_view
definition.description: Load one of your skills (listed under <available_skills> in your instructions). Returns the skill's instructions and its files — follow the instructions to do the task. Load a skill BEFORE starting a task it matches. Pass `path` to read one of the skill's files (e.g. references/format.md).

name.description: The skill name, exactly as listed in <available_skills>

path.description: Optional: a file inside the skill to read instead of its instructions

definition.name: skill_manage
definition.description: Create, change or delete a skill (a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter `name` + `description`, then instructions; optional extra files such as scripts/ and references/). Follow the skill-creator skill when you have it. Actions: create (content, files?) · rewrite (name, content, files? — replaces SKILL.md, and all files when given) · patch (name, old_string, new_string, path? — exact replacement in SKILL.md or a file) · write_file (name, path, content) · remove_file (name, path) · delete (name). Each call asks the user for approval.

name.description: The skill to change (every action except create)

content.description: create/rewrite: the full SKILL.md text; write_file: the file content

files.description: create/rewrite: extra files of the skill

path.description: patch/write_file/remove_file: a file in the skill (patch defaults to SKILL.md)

old_string.description: patch: exact text to replace — must occur exactly once

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read a text file from your workspace. Lines are prefixed with their line number and a tab (not part of the file — never copy that prefix into edit_file). Returns at most 97.7 KB; for bigger files read a range with start_line/end_line.

path.description: File path, relative to your working directory (e.g. "src/app.ts") or under /workspace/shared

definition.name: write_file
definition.description: Create a file, or replace a file's entire content, in your workspace. Parent folders are created. To change part of an existing file use edit_file instead. The write is verified by reading the file back.

path.description: File path, relative to your working directory (e.g. "reports/summary.md") or under /workspace/shared

content.description: The complete new content of the file

definition.name: edit_file
definition.description: Change part of a file in your workspace by replacing an exact piece of text. old_text must match the file exactly (including whitespace, without read_file's line-number prefix) and be unique — include enough surrounding lines, or set replace_all to change every occurrence. The edit is verified by reading the file back.

old_text.description: Exact text currently in the file

new_text.description: Text to put in its place (may be empty to delete)

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

definition.name: list_files
definition.description: List the files and folders in a folder of your workspace (default: your working directory). Use recursive to see a whole tree. "/workspace/shared" holds files shared with other agents.

path.description: Folder to list (default: your working directory)

max_entries.description: Most entries to return (default and max 500)

definition.name: search_files
definition.description: Search the contents of files in your workspace. Returns matching lines as path:line: text. Plain text by default; set regex for a regular expression. Narrow with path and glob (e.g. "*.md").

pattern.description: Text (or regular expression when regex is true) to look for

path.description: Folder or file to search (default: your working directory)

regex.description: Treat pattern as a JavaScript regular expression (default false)

max_matches.description: Most matches to return (default and max 100)

definition.name: terminal
definition.description: Run a shell command in your sandbox (Linux) and get its exit code and output — e.g. build, test, git, file conversions. Starts in your working directory. No network unless the sandbox allows it. Default timeout 120 s; long output is shortened to its start and end. Do not start interactive programs or servers that never exit.

command.description: The command line, e.g. "npm test" or "ls -la src | head"

cwd.description: Directory to run in (default: your working directory)

timeout_seconds.description: Kill the command after this many seconds (max 600)

secrets.description: Names of your secrets to pass as environment variables of the same name (read them as $NAME; never print them)

definition.name: run_code
definition.description: Run a short program in your sandbox and get its output — python (python3), javascript (node) or shell (sh). Runs in your working directory, so it can read and write your workspace files. Print what you need to see. Default timeout 120 s.

cwd.description: Directory to run in (default: your working directory)

timeout_seconds.description: Kill the program after this many seconds (max 600)

secrets.description: Names of your secrets to pass as environment variables of the same name (read them as $NAME; never print them)

definition.name: save_artifact
definition.description: Save a lasting output — a report, a spec section, a takeoff, an estimate — as an artifact the user keeps and can hand to another agent. Artifacts track a file in your workspace, versioned by name, so later turns refer to them by name instead of re-pasting their content. Pass "from_path" to track a file you already wrote (write_file first), or "content" to have it written to artifacts/<name> in your workspace and tracked. Use one or the other, not both.

name.description: Stable name, unique for this agent (e.g. "clash-report.md" or "reports/q3-takeoff.csv")

type.description: MIME type ("text/markdown", "text/csv", "text/html", "application/json") or a domain type ("aec/takeoff", "aec/clash-report"). A real MIME type lets the user's Artifacts panel render it (formatted markdown, a table, a rendered page) instead of plain text.

content.description: Text to write to your workspace and track. Leave it out when you use from_path.

from_path.description: Instead of content: a workspace file to track (its bytes are not copied). Leave it out when you pass content — content wins if both are given.

description.description: One line on what this artifact is, for the user's list

note.description: Why this version exists — shown in the version history

definition.name: update_artifact
definition.description: Record a new version of a tracked artifact. Identify it by "name" or "id", then give either the complete new content (not a patch) in "content" (rewrites the tracked file), or a different workspace file to track with "from_path" — one or the other, not both. Give neither to record the tracked file's current state after you edited it yourself with edit_file/write_file.

name.description: Name of the artifact to update (or use id)

id.description: Id of the artifact to update (or use name)

content.description: The complete new content, written to the tracked file. Leave it out to track without rewriting.

from_path.description: Instead of content: a different workspace file to track from now on. Leave it out when you pass content — content wins if both are given.

note.description: What changed in this version — shown in the version history

expected_version.description: Only update if this is still the current version number; otherwise the call fails

definition.name: read_artifact
definition.description: Read an artifact's tracked file, live from your workspace. Use this instead of keeping a long deliverable in the conversation: refer to the artifact by name and read it when you need it.

name.description: Name of the artifact (or use id)

id.description: Id of the artifact (or use name)

max_bytes.description: Most bytes of content to return

definition.name: list_artifacts
definition.description: List the artifacts you have made — name, type, version, size and description, newest first. Check this before saving, so you update an existing deliverable instead of creating a near-duplicate.

tags.description: Only artifacts carrying any of these tags

this_session_only.description: Only artifacts first created in this conversation
